short: The general who took elephants over the Alps and beat Rome repeatedly without winning.
full:
Hannibal Barca, born around 247 BCE, took command of Carthaginian forces in Spain at twenty-six. In 218 BCE he marched an army with cavalry and war elephants over the Pyrenees, across the Rhone and through the Alps into Italy, losing perhaps half his men to the crossing. He then destroyed successive Roman armies at the Trebia, at Lake Trasimene and, in 216 BCE, at Cannae, where a double envelopment annihilated a force of some 80,000.

He stayed in Italy for fifteen years without ever taking Rome, which had the manpower to absorb defeat and eventually the sense to avoid pitched battle. Recalled to Africa, he was beaten by Scipio at Zama in 202 BCE, ending the Second Punic War. He served afterwards as a reforming magistrate at Carthage, fled to the Seleucid and then the Bithynian court, and took poison around 183 BCE rather than be handed to Rome. Sabaton's "Lightning at the Gates", from Legends (2025), is about the Alpine crossing.
